script.title: Apollo 13’s Square Peg
script.hook_line: Apollo Thirteen’s crew needed a square peg to fit a round hole to survive.
script.close_line: Square filters kept the lifeboat’s air safe without fitting its round openings.

spine.claim: The Apollo 13 crew’s survival depended in part on finding a way to use the command module’s square carbon dioxide removal canisters with the lunar module’s round openings.

Vance Brand at Mission Control told the Apollo 13 astronauts that a team was working on a procedure to connect the command module’s square lithium hydroxide canisters to the lunar module’s outlet hoses.
Apollo 13’s lunar module was designed to support two astronauts for two days and had to support three astronauts for about four days.

The spare square lithium hydroxide canisters aboard the command module did not fit the round openings in the lunar module’s carbon dioxide removal system. The crew was using the lunar module as a lifeboat and needed the filters to prevent carbon dioxide from reaching deadly levels.

idea_point.hook: Three Apollo astronauts needed NASA to fit a square peg into a round hole.
idea_point.turn: The crew had spare filters within reach, but the hardware they were sheltering in could not take them. Mission Control had to work with what the astronauts already had aboard.
idea_point.payoff: All three astronauts made it home. The lunar module had to support three people for about four days on a design meant for two people for two days.
